action-spectacle.description: Mission: Impossible Fallout, Top Gun Maverick and The Dark Knight are the cinematic equivalent of gripping your armrest. You want practical stunts, globe-hopping chases and heroes who really, truly mean it. Popcorn strongly recommended.
action-spectacle.name: Big-screen adrenaline rushes

antihero-crime-sagas.description: You can't resist watching a good person go wonderfully, terribly wrong. Breaking Bad and Better Call Saul give you moral descent with a side of dark humour and some of the best-written conversations on TV. Albuquerque has never felt so tense.
antihero-crime-sagas.name: Slow slides into darkness

british-crime-drama.description: You like your Britain moody, clever and occasionally very polite. One night it's the grief-soaked tension of Broadchurch and Happy Valley, the next it's Slow Horses and The Night Manager doing spy games in drizzly corridors. And then, because you're a person of range, you cleanse the palate with Paddington 2, Great British Bake Off and a Grand Designs renovation gone gloriously over budget.
mood_states: in the mood for a puzzle
british-crime-drama.name: Proper British Telly

cerebral-sci-fi.description: Arrival, Blade Runner 2049 and Interstellar are the kind of films that make you stare quietly at the ceiling afterwards, and you love that. You like your space and time melancholic, beautiful and just a little heartbreaking. Big ideas, bigger feelings, and a slow, hypnotic pace suit you perfectly.
cerebral-sci-fi.name: Sci-fi that stays with you

class-satire-thrillers.description: Rich families behaving badly is your happy place. Succession's backstabbing boardrooms, Knives Out's delicious whodunit, and Parasite's razor-sharp twist on class all land perfectly with you. You love being entertained and quietly horrified at the same time.
class-satire-thrillers.name: Eat-the-rich entertainment

cozy-whodunits-comedy.description: Only Murders in the Building is your kind of crime: a podcast, a few unlikely friends, and a murder solved with plenty of jokes. You like your mysteries charming and cosy, with the company as important as the culprit.
cozy-whodunits-comedy.name: Cosy mysteries with banter

dark-dramedy.description: The Bear's kitchen is a pressure cooker of grief, family and shouting, and you love every frantic minute. The Grand Budapest Hotel adds its own dollhouse-perfect eccentricity to the mix. You like your stories stylish, messy and secretly tender underneath.
mood_states: in the mood for something sharp
dark-dramedy.name: Chaos with a lot of heart

hindi-cinema-and-series.description: You'll laugh through 3 Idiots, cry through Dangal, and then get properly twisted up by Andhadhun's piano-and-plot-twist madness. Panchayat gives you small-town warmth, while Delhi Crime and Sacred Games pull you into the grittier side. It's a row with big heart and sharp edges, and you're clearly comfortable with both.
hindi-cinema-and-series.name: Hindi stories that feel like home

japanese-stories.description: You wandered into Spirited Away and clearly never fully left the bathhouse. You love a world where nothing is explained too neatly and everything feels a little dreamlike. Miyazaki's strange, tender magic is right up your alley.
japanese-stories.name: Ghibli-style wonder

mind-bending-thrillers.description: You don't just watch Dark, Inception and Severance, you take notes on them. Timelines fold, dreams nest inside dreams, and an office job turns deeply sinister, and you're delighted by every twist. You'd happily draw a family tree on a napkin to keep up.
mind-bending-thrillers.name: Puzzles that bend your brain

nature-design-documentaries.description: Last Week Tonight is your Sunday-night ritual: a deep dive into something outrageous, delivered with fury and jokes in equal measure. You like to feel clued in and laugh at the same time. Learning has never been this entertaining.
members: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver
nature-design-documentaries.name: Smart, funny, informed

space-epics.description: You like your galaxies packed with rebels, empires and very serious men whispering in very large rooms. Andor, Dune and The Expanse give you political chess among the stars, while Shogun brings the same intrigue to feudal Japan. Slow build, huge payoff, and you're here for all of it.
mood_states: ready for a long immersive watch
space-epics.name: Epic worlds, scheming powers

true-story-dramas.description: Chernobyl and Zodiac both prove that real events can be more unsettling than any invention. You like your drama meticulous, bleak and deeply researched, the kind that leaves a pit in your stomach and a dozen tabs open afterwards.
mood_states: ready to go down a rabbit hole
true-story-dramas.name: True stories that haunt

wholesome-feel-good.description: Ted Lasso is basically a warm hug in episode form, and you know it. You're drawn to optimism, good-hearted friendships and the kind of humour that never needs to be cruel. Sometimes the best plan is a very nice man in a moustache believing in you.
wholesome-feel-good.name: Kindness, with a side of football
